subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` as the canonical all-configured-model health check, or fold that behavior into a broader model-safety workflow?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature adds a new live CLI probe mode that affects provider credentials, token/rate-limit behavior, JSON output, and adjacent fallback/migration diagnostics.

options.title: Add Status Probe --all
options.body: Add an opt-in `models status --probe --all` mode that probes configured model candidates while preserving the current one-model-per-provider default.

options.title: Fold Into Model-Safety Workflow
options.body: Make the staged migration or fallback-chain work own configured-model verification so users get one model-safety UX instead of parallel commands.

options.title: Defer Live Probe Expansion
options.body: Keep current provider/auth probes and OpenRouter scan behavior until maintainers want to own the cost and support burden of all-model live probing.

recommendation.title: Add Status Probe --all
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in `models status --probe --all` mode that probes configured model candidates while preserving the current one-model-per-provider default.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current auth-probe surface and has the strongest combined history on the model status/probe and product-boundary decisions.
